sources.title: cmux docs source: coderouter
sources.locator: docs.coderouterOverview (accounts; routing; teams; usage; privacy); source of https://cmux.com/docs/coderouter, which returned a Vercel 403 checkpoint on 2026-11-21
sources.finding: CodeRouter forwards agent requests to pooled ChatGPT, OpenAI key, OpenRouter key, OpenCode Go, Claude Max/Pro token, Anthropic key or Bedrock accounts; sessions stick to a healthy account; on rate limit, rejection or no answer the account enters cooldown and the request retries elsewhere, only before any output streams. The hosted service makes the provider request. Each provider meters its own account. cr shows quota state (--json); cmux coderouter machines shows 30-day tokens and API-equivalent value per machine and usage by day, workspace, agent and model inside a machine; API-equivalent value is an estimate, not a bill. Credentials encrypted; Cloud machines hold none (edge-injected, machine-bound, revoked on delete). Responses carry x-coderouter-request-id. Requires cmux sign-in.

sources.title: cmux Cloud
sources.locator: Early access note; What a machine is; What you need; Steps
sources.finding: Deployed page (matches docs.cloudOverview in the v0.65.2.2 source; no cmux NEXT wording): cmux Cloud is in early access and available unless the organization disables it; turn on Settings > Beta Features > Cloud Machines. A machine is a persistent cloud computer that belongs to you or to your team; every machine runs the cmux TUI daemon, which holds its workspaces and terminals, so closing a pane never stops the process. Requirements: a paid cmux plan (free accounts cannot create machines); no VPN, SSH key or port forwarding setup. Sign in from the Cloud tab or login command; create with File > New Cloud Machine or Shift-Cmd-Y; Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode and Pi are preinstalled; the same steps work from the CLI.

sources.title: cmux Cloud machines
sources.locator: Create; Plan limits; Keep coding agents up to date; Pause and resume; Checkpoints, forks, and restore; Delete; When your plan ends
sources.finding: Deployed page (matches docs.cloudMachines in the v0.65.2.2 source): a retried cmux vm new reuses the same request; failed creates offer retry, show or copy the error. Free accounts cannot create machines. Pro and Founder's Edition: up to 5 active machines (running or starting) sharing 20 vCPU/40 GB; Team: 5 active machines per paid seat, each seat adds 20 vCPU/40 GB; Max: 5 active machines sharing 80 vCPU/160 GB. Paused machines do not use the pool; over-pool requests are refused with pool usage shown. "There is no metering and no overage billing." Agent updates come from sha256-verified GitHub releases; a failed check runs again on next connect. Machines do not pause when idle; pause stops processes and keeps disk and history. Checkpoint and Fork appear only where the provider supports them. Delete is permanent, removes public URLs and revokes model access. After a paid plan ends, machines older than 7 days lock; files are kept.

Auto-Connect discovers compatible Macs signed in to the same account without Tailscale, yet the page also says "cmux does not provide networking out of the box" and that cmux does not proxy or relay terminal traffic. Notification forwarding sends title and body through cmux servers and Apple push unless Hide content is on. The terminal session flows directly between phone and Mac and is not stored on cmux servers. The unreleased d421b4b docs source names cmux Pro instead of Founder's Edition.

sources.finding: Free $0 (open-source macOS terminal, CLI agents with your own keys). One rendering of the page also lists Plus $15/mo (1 saved VM including paused machines, 2-8 vCPU, 4-16 GiB RAM, 16-128 GiB disk, no monthly hour cap). Pro $50/mo or $480/yr (up to 5 Cloud VMs sharing 20 vCPU/40 GB; the cmux iOS app and email support); Max $200/mo or $1,920/yr (5 VMs sharing 80 vCPU/160 GB; the iOS app); Team $60/user/mo (5 VMs per paid seat); Enterprise custom (self-hosted Cloud, SSO and SAML, audit logs, SOC 2 and an SLA). The comparison counts "Saved Cloud VMs, including paused machines". FAQ: the iOS app pairs with the Mac over the built-in cmux iroh network; Free accounts do not include Cloud VMs. "Already paid? Connect Founder's Edition".
